title: Filtered ring colimits commute with fixed-monoid unit pushouts
statement:
Let $I$ be a small filtered category: it is nonempty, every pair of objects has a common target, and every pair of parallel arrows is equalized by an arrow out of their target. Work in a universe containing $I$ and all coefficient sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B:I\to\mathrm{CRing}$ be a diagram of commutative unital rings with unital transition homomorphisms, and let $A=\varinjlim_I B_i$ be its ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with maps $b_i:B_i\to A$. Let $R$ be any commutative monoid and let $\beta_i:R\to(B_i,\cdot)$ be compatible monoid homomorphisms, inducing $\beta:R\to(A,\cdot)$. Put $E_i=\beta_i^{-1}(B_i^\times)$ and $E=\beta^{-1}(A^\times)$.

Every unit of $A$ is $b_i(u)$ for some $u\in B_i^\times$. Two unit representatives having the same image in $A^\times$ become equal after maps to a common stage. For every $i$ and $e\in R$, $\beta(e)$ is a unit if and only if there is an arrow $i\to j$ with $e\in E_j$. These assertions require no finite generation or cancellation assumption on $R$.

Define $P_i$ as the quotient of $R\times B_i^\times$ by the commutative-monoid congruence generated by $(re,u)\sim(r,\beta_i(e)u)$ for $e\in E_i$, and define $Q$ as the quotient of $R\times A^\times$ by $(re,a)\sim(r,\beta(e)a)$ for $e\in E$. Transition maps on unit representatives induce a diagram $P_i$. The set colimit $\varinjlim_I |P_i|$ carries a canonical commutative-monoid structure, with multiplication computed at any common stage. The canonical map
$$\varinjlim_I |P_i|\longrightarrow Q,\qquad [[r,u]_i]\longmapsto[r,b_i(u)]$$
is an isomorphism of commutative monoids. Its inverse sends $[r,a]$ to the class of $[r,u]_i$ for any unit representative $b_i(u)=a$; it is independent of that representative and of the displayed pushout relations. The isomorphism preserves the images of $R$ and the canonical maps from all $B_i^\times$.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits: eventual equality and simultaneous finite representatives; agent-formulated unit-pushout consequence used at etale geometric stalks (Tag 03PQ, lemma-cofinal-etale).

proof.text: Record explicitly how filteredness will be used. A finite list of objects has a common target, by induction using the common-target axiom; an empty list is handled by nonemptiness. Given finitely many arrows between these objects, first choose maps of all objects into one target. For each specified arrow, the two composites from its source to that target are parallel; postcompose to equalize them, repeating for the finite list. Equalities obtained earlier persist under postcomposition. Thus any finite diagram admits maps to a common target commuting with its specified arrows. This uses the equalization axiom, not uniqueness of arrows in $I$.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $x\in B_i$ whose image $b_i(x)$ is a unit, and let $a$ be its inverse in $A$. The first clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] supplies $y\in B_k$ with $b_k(y)=a$. Move $x,y$ to one stage $l$, along $i\to l$ and $k\to l$. Their product $z$ has image $1$. Clause (2) applied to $z,1\in B_l$ supplies $f,g:l\to m$ with $B(f)(z)=B(g)(1)=1$. Hence the images of $x,y$ along $f$ multiply to $1$, so the image of $x$ is a unit in the commutative ring $B_m$. Conversely every ring homomorphism maps a unit and its inverse to a unit and its inverse. An arbitrary unit of $A$ first has a ring-element representative by clause (1), and this argument makes it a unit representative at a later stage. Apply the same argument with $x=\beta_i(e)$ to prove, for every prescribed $i$, that $\beta(e)$ is a unit exactly when $e\in E_j$ after some arrow $i\to j$. No property of $R$ enters.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: If units $u\in B_i^\times$ and $v\in B_j^\times$ have the same image in $A^\times$, their underlying ring elements have the same image. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] gives arrows $i\to k,j\to k$ where those ring elements agree. The induced units agree too: an inverse to a given element of a monoid is unique, so equality of underlying elements is equality of units. This proves the claimed eventual equality for unit representatives.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: For $t:i\to j$, compatibility of $\beta_i$ gives $\beta_j(e)=B(t)(\beta_i(e))$. Thus $E_i\subseteq E_j$. The homomorphism $(r,u)\mapsto(r,B(t)(u))$ sends each generating relation $(re,u)\sim(r,\beta_i(e)u)$ to the corresponding relation at $j$. Its kernel congruence therefore contains the generated congruence, and it descends to a homomorphism $P_i\to P_j$. The identity and composition laws hold on every representative $(r,u)$, so these are a diagram. The same calculation for $b_i$ gives compatible monoid maps $q_i:P_i\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: Write $C=\varinjlim_I|P_i|$ and $c_i:|P_i|\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] every element is $c_i(p)$, and equality is witnessed by arrows to a common stage. Define $c_i(p)c_j(q)=c_k(P(f)(p)P(g)(q))$ for $f:i\to k,g:j\to k$, and $1_C=c_i(1)$ for any $i$. To compare two choices of representatives and target, use the equality witnesses from that cited node for each replaced representative, and then Step 1 for the finite diagram consisting of the chosen arrows and these witnesses. At that stage both products are the same product of the same two elements. This proves independence; the same argument proves independence of $1_C$. For three elements choose one common stage: associativity there proves associativity in $C$; commutativity and the unit laws follow at a common stage as well. The $c_i$ are homomorphisms, since their products and units can be computed at $i$. The compatible $q_i$ consequently induce a homomorphism $F:C\to Q$, with $F(c_i([r,u]_i))=[r,b_i(u)]$.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: For $r\in R$ and $a\in A^\times$ define $H(r,a)=c_i([r,u]_i)$ using a unit representative $b_i(u)=a$ from Step 2. Step 3 puts any two such representatives at a common stage with equal units, where the pairs with fixed first coordinate $r$ are identical. Hence $H$ is independent of the representative. Given $(r,a),(s,b)$, move unit representatives $u,v$ to one common stage $k$. The pair $(rs,uv)$ represents $(rs,ab)$, so the definition of multiplication in Step 5 gives $H(rs,ab)=H(r,a)H(s,b)$. The representative $1\in B_i^\times$ gives $H(1,1)=1_C$. Thus $H:R\times A^\times\to C$ is a monoid homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: For a generating relation of $Q$, fix $e\in E$, $r\in R$ and $a\in A^\times$. Choose a unit representative $u\in B_i^\times$ of $a$. By the prescribed-starting-stage assertion in Step 2 there is $t:i\to j$ with $e\in E_j$. Put $u'=B(t)(u)$. Then $H(re,a)=c_j([re,u']_j)=c_j([r,\beta_j(e)u']_j)=H(r,\beta(e)a)$. The middle equality is exactly a defining relation of $P_j$. The kernel of the monoid homomorphism $H$ is a congruence containing every generating relation of $Q$, hence contains the congruence they generate. Therefore $H$ descends to a homomorphism $G:Q\to C$. This checks all congruence consequences, without assuming that equality in $Q$ is a single generating relation.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality description after Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written unit and monoid-quotient application.

proof.text: For $[r,a]\in Q$, choose $u\in B_i^\times$ representing $a$; then $FG([r,a])=[r,b_i(u)]=[r,a]$. Conversely every element of $C$ is $c_i(p)$ by the set-colimit representative assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], and every $p\in P_i$ is $[r,u]_i$ by its definition as a quotient. Choosing this very $u$ in the definition of $H$ gives $GF(c_i([r,u]_i))=c_i([r,u]_i)$. Hence $F,G$ are inverse monoid homomorphisms. In particular $G$ has exactly the asserted formula and independence properties. The image of $r\in R$ in $C$ is $c_i([r,1]_i)$, independent of $i$ by a common target, and $F$ maps it to $[r,1]$. For $u\in B_i^\times$, $F(c_i([1,u]_i))=[1,b_i(u)]$. These are the required compatibilities.
